g.text: Worked example: your app in Sydney calls Claude Opus 5.5. Same per-token price on both endpoints; the features differ.
AWS's recommended default for new apps
in-region only · fewer models and regions
Responses API: sync only, no server-side tools
Responses API: full, incl. background=true and server tools
Cross-Region inference: au. · apac. · global. profiles
Guardrails, e.g. mask PII before it reaches the model
Application inference profiles → cost per team
Async jobs for long-running agent work
Projects and Workspaces → usage per team
One TPM quota per model, input + output combined
max_tokens is reserved when the request starts
No RPM limit · attribute by IAM principal, tags,
Separate input TPM and output TPM
Fair-share scheduling: requests may briefly queue
Higher initial limits · no RPM limit
SigV4 or Bedrock API key · client-side tool use · prompt caching (mantle: model-dependent) · stateful conversations · identical per-token price
Inference on an AWS serving fleet
AWS Trainium chips + NVIDIA GPUs · weights and KV cache held in HBM
Choose on capability, not cost. Model access is per account: "is not available for this account" is a Model access issue, not IAM or code.
From a VPC, use PrivateLink interface endpoints to avoid NAT egress charges.
